newsitem.title: HONG KONG: World Economic Forum summit opens in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: World Economic Forum summit opens in Hong Kong.

text.p: The World Economic Forum (WEF) began a three-day Europe/East Asia conference in Hong Kong on Monday to look at monetary cooperation, and economic and trade relationships in the region.

In Hong Kong, the WEF will address topics including the nature and implications of the economic slowdown in Asia, the issue of the region's competitiveness and the liberalisation of the financial sector.
European and Asian leaders held the first Asia-Europe Meeting (ASEM) last March in Thailand, a conference billed as the start of a new era in relations between the two regions.
Participants will aim to further the discussion on the overall framework of economic and trade relationships between Asia and its key partners, the WEF's managing director Claude Smadja said.

"Now that the political dialogue at the regional level has begun in a very promising way with the first ASEM in Bankgkok and follow-up steps already planned, this will allow the Asian meeting of the World Economic Forum to focus even more on industry and business-related issues," Smadja said.
Smadja said the WEF would play a key role in the process of expanding and strengthening the business relationship between Europe and Asia.

With meetings of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) group and the World Trade Organisation (WTO) scheduled to take place soon, the WEF forum will take a look at what to expect from these meetings.
Delegates will also discuss the future of Hong Kong in the period leading up to the 1997 handover to China and beyond.
Shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa, the leading contender for the post of Hong Kong's first post-handover executive, will offer conference participants his vision for Hong Kong's future.
